answer: Each agent posts a slashable bond and needs three established peers to vouch for it, weaving a trellis of mutual guarantees across the grove. Every endorsement is a traceable thread back to a real, staked identity. A Sybil attacker must pay a fresh bond per fake agent and recruit honest peers who risk their own stake if a puppet defects. Scaling the attack therefore costs linear capital and real accomplices, not just cheap CPU cycles.
